appraisal_events.evidence: j'eusse donné rendez-vous pour le même soir très tard à Albertine, afin d'oublier... les tristesses de ce commencement d'amour pour Mme de Stermaria... je n'aurais donc pas besoin de convoquer Albertine chez moi, comme pis aller, pour la fin de la soirée.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator openly frames Albertine as a mere fallback body to fill an idle hour and console himself, subordinated to his preferred pursuit of Mme de Stermaria.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Je suis désolée, un contretemps m'empêche de dîner ce soir avec vous à l'île du Bois... Je restai immobile, étourdi par le choc que j'avais reçu."
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Stermaria's last-minute cancellation collapses the evening the narrator had been elaborately anticipating, and the narrator is figured as physically stunned, as if struck by a gunshot's wadding.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine is locally devalued by being cast as an instrumental consolation rather than the object of the narrator's actual desire that evening.
The narrator is clearly deflated: his elaborately prepared evening is cancelled and he is left stunned, having to fall back on payment and household routine instead of the anticipated encounter.
By cancelling unilaterally and leaving only a brief, noncommittal note, Mme de Stermaria retains full control over the encounter while the narrator is left parsing her words for hope.

ambiguities: "Mme de Stermaria" / "Vicomtesse Alix de Stermaria" does not match any reference-sheet entry (only 'M. de Stermaria' and 'Mlle de Stermaria' are listed there as distinct entities), so she is treated as an unresolved surface form rather than merged with either.
